extracted.intended_audience: research chemists and biochemists; academic researchers in organic chemistry and enzymology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative principles for conducting biochemical and organic-chemical research: emphasis on combining synthetic chemistry, analytical methods, stereochemical considerations, enzyme isolation, and biologically relevant experimental conditions to elucidate structures and mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ultimate aim of biochemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate aim of biochemistry is to gain complete insight into the unending series of changes which attend plant and animal metabolism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplishing this requires 'complete knowledge of each individual chemical substance occurring in the cycle of changes' and analytical methods capable of recognizing those substances under living conditions; research should be directed toward mapping the full series of metabolic transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical recognition under living conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical methods which will permit of its recognition under conditions such as exist in the living organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop sensitive analytical techniques able to follow changes in situ (for example, within chlorophyll granules) rather than relying solely on destructive laboratory assays; improved biological/analytical coupling is required to elucidate assimilation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of synthetic chemistry in elucidation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the office of organic chemistry, especially of synthetic chemistry, to accumulate this absolutely essential material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use synthesis to establish constitution and properties of natural substances (examples: Berthelot and Wurtz on glycerine; synthesis of amino acids and polypeptides); synthetic reproductions provide proof of structure and supply material for analytical study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mimic natural processes using mild, biologically relevant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory methods are doubtless altogether different from those which come into operation in the living world; chemists are trying to effect changes by 'mild interactions' under conditions comparable with those which prevail in the living organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust experimental conditions (milder reagents, catalysts, light-driven reactions, enzymatic-like catalysis) to better approximate in vivo conditions—cite Fenton reduction, catalytic processes, and light-action studies as relevant directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for stereochemistry and asymmetry in biosyntheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The asymmetric character of the synthesis: according to present experience ... the optically active hexoses of the d-series, glucose and fructose, are alone formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attempting to imitate biological syntheses, explicitly incorporate stereochemical/asymmetric factors (possible asymmetric complexes, chiral constituents of chlorophyll granules, stereoselective pathways) into hypotheses and synthetic strategies; consider additive complexes and induced asymmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop improved separation and differentiation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: As the methods differentiating and separating them are improved, the number [of carbohydrate species] will be largely increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in better chromatographic, crystallographic, and separation techniques because many monosaccharides/disaccharides and protein components are currently only partially resolved or appear as mixed crystals; improved methods will reveal greater diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use degradation (hydrolysis) and synthesis to determine protein constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the numerous attempts to unravel the constitution of the proteins by analytical means, the only method which has given us useful results hitherto is that of hydrolysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine hydrolytic degradation to identify component amino acids with forward synthesis (the reverse process) to recreate polypeptides; validate structural conclusions from degradation by successful synthesis of analogous compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve synthetic racemates into optically active amino acids
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of glycine, all the amino-acids derived from natural sources are optically active; when prepared by ordinary synthetic methods they are obtained in the first instance in the racemic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply resolution methods (recrystallisation, partial fermentation, acyl-derivative approaches) to obtain the natural enantiomeric forms; prefer or develop synthetic routes that yield optically active products or effective resolution procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruct proteins from major cleavage products (polypeptide synthesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work can be restricted to the reconstruction of the original system from the major products of cleavage formed in the process of hydrolytic dissection. Synthetic products (polypeptides) resembling proteins have already been prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identified major hydrolytic fragments as building blocks for synthetic assembly of polypeptides (e.g., octadecarpeptide examples) to approach the structure of natural proteins; target simpler proteins (silk fibroin) before attempting the full proteome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate and characterize enzymes (composition and specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: We know practically nothing of the composition of the enzymes, as the complete isolation of an enzyme has never been accomplished. The specific character of their action ... favours the assumption that enzyme and hydrolyte enter temporarily into combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to isolate enzymes to homogeneity and determine their composition; characterize mechanisms of action (binding, zymogen activation, cofactor effects) and quantify specificity through binding and activity studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use synthetic analogues to probe enzymatic activity and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The artificial glucosides have been of use in establishing the dependence of the action of enzymes on configuration; the synthesised polypeptides are now being used ... to define and measure the activity of the proteoclasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and employ synthetic substrates, glucosides, and polypeptide analogues to test enzyme substrate-specificity, stereochemical dependence, and to develop assays measuring proteolytic or other enzymatic activities (examples: work by Abderhalden, Euler, Bertrand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply stereochemical and structural approaches to complex biological molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: The synthetic exploration of the purine group has served to direct recent observations ... Structural chemistry is slowly acquiring the mastery over cholesterol by making use of the experience afforded by the synthetic study of the hydroaromatic substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted synthetic programs and stereochemical analysis to elucidate structures and reaction pathways of purines, lecithins, cholesterol, alkaloids, terpenes, and other complex biomolecules; leverage synthetic insights to interpret biochemical transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize natural heterogeneity (mixed crystals, isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: It cannot be decided from their crystalline appearance whether the products are definite substances, as the tendency to mixed crystals is the greater the more complicated the molecule ... it would therefore be altogether surprising if the crystallised natural proteins should turn out to be single substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for isomorphism and mixed-crystal phenomena when interpreting crystalline data; avoid assuming single-substance identity from crystal habit—use complementary analyses to detect mixtures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base theory on observed facts; avoid preconceived opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to imitate the great example of Faraday, who ... directed his attention to actual phenomena without allowing himself to be influenced by preconceived opinion, and who in his theoretical conceptions gave expression only to observed facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate hypotheses grounded strictly in empirical observation; resist letting prevailing dogma or speculative extrapolation override reproducible data—prioritize experimental verification.
